messages:
laura (sec-eng): Heads-up — found an RBAC regression: gpu-pool-controller SA can impersonate a wide set of serviceAccounts (kube-system) after last infra deploy. Repro steps below. Please triage.

marc (eng-infra): Thanks for the ping. when did the change land?

laura (sec-eng): Rolled 2026-03-08 22:14 UTC via PR #1934 (infra/kube-deploy). Diff shows a ClusterRoleBinding applied to sa:gpu-pool-controller with verbs including impersonate.

jess (eng-runtime): linking audit events — audit-bot flagged many impersonate requests from that SA to other SAs and nodes.

audit-bot: Detected 24 suspicious impersonation events from serviceAccount:gpu-pool-controller -> serviceAccount:kube-system:node-problem-detector at 2026-03-09T01:02:11Z. See internal alert IMP-1781.

deploy-bot: Last deploy for infra/kube-deploy happened at 2026-03-08T22:14:03Z by user:marc. CI job: deploy-infra-23.

anil (oncall): Immediate mitigation: remove the binding and rotate the SA token. I'll run commands now.

anil (oncall): ran: ```bash
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding gpu-pool-controller-crb
kubectl -n infra delete rolebinding gpu-pool-controller-rb || true
```

laura (sec-eng): Good. After removal, confirm there are no live impersonation events and rotate any keys/tokens. Also we need to check KMS IAM bindings referenced by that SA.

marc (eng-infra): I've pulled IAM policy: sa/gpu-pool-controller had roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter via a broad group binding (automation-service-accounts). I'm removing the KMS role now and narrowing the group.

marc (eng-infra): ran: ```bash
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \\
  --member="serviceAccount:gpu-pool-controller@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \\
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"```

jess (eng-runtime): We need a least-priv Role for the GPU controller. Proposed Role (namespaced) — allow viewing pods, creating leases, reading node objects but NO "impersonate" or broad iam perms.

laura (sec-eng): Please paste a minimal YAML.

jess (eng-runtime): ```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: gpu-pool-controller-role
  namespace: infra
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","pods/exec","nodes","endpoints"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch","create","update"]
- apiGroups: ["coordination.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["leases"]
  verbs: ["create","get","update"]
```

marc (eng-infra): Also adding an OPA admission gate to block creation of ClusterRoleBinding that grant cluster-admin to serviceAccounts created by automation. Draft rego in infra repo.

anil (oncall): I ran a quick grep across clusters for existing problematic bindings: found 2 other clusters with similar binding — patching them.

laura (sec-eng): Created SEC-412 (postmortem + remediation checklist). Items: 1) rotate SA keys, 2) remove KMS binding, 3) apply least-priv Role + RoleBinding, 4) add OPA policy + CI gate, 5) add alert for new cluster-admin CRBs. Assign @jess and @marc.

jess (eng-runtime): Opening PR to replace the clusterRole with the namespaced Role + RoleBinding and add test: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1982 (draft). Includes unit test for RBAC lint rule.

marc (eng-infra): Also updated cloud IAM docs: removed automation-service-accounts group from KMS key ACLs and created a dedicated service account with scoped KMS access for the GPU encryption key.

anil (oncall): After removal I see no more impersonation events in last 30m. Rotating SA tokens now and bumping secrets.

laura (sec-eng): Follow-ups: timeline for EOD — rotate SA credentials, merge PR to infra, deploy OPA gate to staging, add alert in prometheus for clusterrolebinding creations.

sally (security-manager): Noted. Please prepare a short blameless summary for execs and affected teams (SRE, Platform). Keep me posted on rollout status.

marc (eng-infra): Postmortem draft: /docs/ops/sec/SEC-412-draft.md. Will include root cause: unintended clusterRoleBinding from automation change + no CI gate.

laura (sec-eng): Thanks all. We'll close once PR merged, SA rotated, and OPA gate in place. :lock:
